title: National Securities Depository Ltd - 544467 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: NSDL Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 7.9% YoY to INR89.1 crores, with EBITDA margin at 57.8% amid front-loaded tech and manpower spend.
summary.overview: Standalone total income grew 15.3% YoY to INR219.7 crores and PAT rose 7.9% to INR89.1 crores, while management flagged margin moderation from front-loaded technology and hiring. Consolidated total income rose 61.6% YoY to INR560.5 crores, but consolidated PAT grew a slower 9.7% to INR98.3 crores, with the payments bank's one-time onboarding revenue carrying low margins. Demat additions improved: NSDL's incremental market share in net demat account additions rose to 17.6% from about 15.5% a year earlier, with 12.4 lakh net additions. Management stressed that YoY comparison is more meaningful than QoQ given seasonality in e-voting and subsidiary dividends.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR106 crores for full FY26

segments.name: Depository (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue INR182.2 crores (+13.2% YoY); standalone profit is about 91% of consolidated profit. Demat accounts on NSDL reached 4.56 crores, with 12.4 lakh net additions versus 10.4 lakh a year earlier.

segments.name: NSDL Payments Bank (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Drove consolidated revenue growth but margins were diluted by upfront onboarding revenue sharing with a partner on a specific card-led project. Retail customers rose 1.7x YoY to 49.5 lakh from 28.3 lakh; ranked 6th as payee PSP among top 15 banks as of June 30, 2026.

segments.name: NSDL Database Management (NDML)
segments.commentary: Includes KRA, SEZ online and insurance repository businesses. KRA income fell about 2% YoY despite a 20% cut in KYC fetch charges, offset by SEZ growth. Insurance repository business is being moved into a separate subsidiary per IRDAI guidance.

guidance_outlook: Management expects operating leverage to support normalised margins as front-loaded technology and manpower investments mature over the medium term; no near-term margin figure given.
Payments bank: onboarding peak was in Q1; management said Q2 should normalise toward Q4 levels, with transaction-led profitability improving later. Chandok explicitly said this is not guidance.
Hiring to slow ('very cautious') after the FY26 build-out; recently hired staff's cost to flow into coming quarters.
Management remains optimistic on DP-led account growth, contingent on market conditions; new DP ramp-ups expected to flow over time.
Priorities for next year: residual technology modernisation, automation, resilience and customer-experience enhancements.
capex_capacity: Technology spend split into four areas: resilience (regulatory and market overlap), customer experience, automation/AI/ML, and infrastructure refresh on a 5-8 year cycle.
Technology capitalisation was only INR7-8 crores in Q1 FY27 versus INR106 crores for full FY26.
Board approved investment in IIBH, a GIFT City associate in which NSDL holds 20%.
Over 40 APIs launched for DPs in earlier quarters; focus this quarter was driving utilisation.
Depository participants at 317, with 6 DPs added in Q1 FY27 (21 added in FY26).
demand_pricing: Industry demat count crossed 23.16 crore (+16.3% YoY); about 70 lakh new accounts added in Q1 FY27 versus 67 lakh a year earlier.
NSDL incremental market share in net demat additions rose to 17.6% from about 14% in Q4 FY26 and 15.5% in Q1 FY26.
Yuva and Women's Demat plans (zero settlement charges for first 3 years) account for 18-20% of incremental additions.
FinTech share of new account additions rose to about 20%, from about 2% a few quarters ago.
Pledge income grew with pledge/unpledge count up about 15% YoY; unlisted company market share about 70%+; e-voting market share 64% vs 61%; e-voting events 900 vs 794.

Annual custody fees benefited from about 60,000 companies onboarded over FY25-FY26 (33,000 and 30,000); folio count about 14 crore vs 11.9 crore a year earlier. Q1 onboarding was 3,600 companies at INR15,000 per company joining fee (about INR5-6 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Are employee costs (up about 40% on standalone) near peak run-rate, and where is headcount being added?
qa_highlights.answer: Jigar Shah said most FY26 hiring (net about 98 employees in the prior year) is now flowing through costs; hiring will be 'very cautious' from here, with recent recruits' costs hitting coming quarters. Adds were mainly in technology and cybersecurity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payments bank arrangement behind the revenue jump, and is the current run-rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Vijay Chandok said it is a specific card-related project where onboarding joining fees are largely passed through to a partner, so margins are low. Onboarding peaked in Q1 and Q2 should normalise toward Q4 levels; he explicitly said this is not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the tech spend regulator-driven or market-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Chandok split spend into four areas: resilience (regulatory and market overlap, a sizable area), customer experience (mainly market-driven), automation/AI/ML (internal), and infrastructure refresh on a 5-7 to 8 year cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the annual custody fee growth and folio count?
qa_highlights.answer: Jigar Shah said about 33,000 companies were onboarded in FY25 and 30,000 in FY26; folio count is about 14 crore versus 11.9 crore a year earlier. Market share in unlisted companies is about 70%+.

qa_highlights.question: What drove pledge income growth and KYC income resilience at NDML?
qa_highlights.answer: Shah attributed pledge growth to MTF book activity and pledge/unpledge counts up about 15% YoY. Chandok said the 20% KRA fetch-charge cut was partly offset by SEZ growth, and NDML subsidiary split would not be shared yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the fintech share of new accounts jumped from about 2% to about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Chandok said work over the last several quarters (customer meetings, back-office vendor workshops, features, relationship building) led to about 4-month onboarding per fintech; ramp-ups are gradual and accelerating, with more fintechs now in the journey.

qa_highlights.question: What were the major hits and misses since the CEO joined and what are next-year priorities?
qa_highlights.answer: Chandok cited four themes: technology modernisation (largely done at basic level), skills/leadership gap (largely complete), market penetration (good progress), and IPO completed in 7 months. Next focus is residual tech modernisation, automation, resilience and customer experience.

qa_highlights.question: Are DPs onboarded in the last year converting to demat accounts, and what is the DP ramp timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Chandok said DP onboarding takes about 12-16 weeks; the 21 DPs added in FY26 are exclusively on NSDL, so accounts flow to NSDL once live, and many are in integration or early scale-up. Expected benefit is contingent on market conditions.

risks_watch: Standalone margin moderation from front-loaded technology and manpower spend; management has given no near-term margin figure.
Payments bank profitability: Q1 onboarding joining fees were largely pass-through to a partner; Q2 normalisation and transaction-led margin recovery are unproven.
Sustainability of pledge income growth, which depends on MTF book trends and broker activity.
KRA/NDML revenue pressure from the 20% KYC fetch-charge cut; subsidiary-level revenue split not disclosed.
Fintech ramp-up pace (about 20% of new additions) and DP conversion depend on market conditions; management was cautious on outcomes.
Insurance repository business being moved to a separate subsidiary per IRDAI guidance; transition underway with timing and cost unspecified.
Geopolitical and crude price risks revived in July 2026 after the West Asia easing in Q1.

We have front loaded these investments in manpower and technology to strengthen adequacy of resources and to support infrastructure and future growth.
So, please do not take it away as any kind of a guidance. I want to make it explicit.
So, it's virtually a pass through. So therefore, the margins are low there.
summary.management_tone: Confident on market share, account additions and DP pipeline, but cautious and explicitly non-committal on the payments bank run-rate and on forward margins. Management repeatedly declined to share subsidiary-level details and steered investors to YoY rather than QoQ comparisons.

adds.what: IIBH GIFT City associate investment (NSDL holds 20%); board approved, not a capacity addition

growth.why: Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew 13.2% YoY, but no revenue growth guidance is given, hiring is slowing to 'very cautious', technology capitalisation fell to INR7-8 crore from INR106 crore in FY26, and the only capacity item is a board-approved IIBH investment rather than company-owned capacity.
